player.name: Pip Marrowby
player.concept: a gnome tinkerer with a head full of side projects

established: Cob accepts the copper bet and throws a stone.
The pigeon is startled off the beam and lands in the yard.
Cob has rejected the offered trade and moved toward the water butt.
Moll has taught Pip the Saltmere dock-cant curse “Brenn’s barn.”

opened.title: J. Sallow and the Purveyor's office

rulings.act: Bets Cob to hit the pigeon with a stone
rulings.why: it costs them nothing (trivial, strong, hostile)
rulings.changed: Cob grins at the copper and takes careful aim. His stone clips the beam beside the pigeon; it flaps down into the yard, startled and unharmed, while Prout keeps turning untouched

rulings.act: Trade the clockwork cricket for another way into the loft
rulings.changed: Cob laughs at the half-disassembled cricket and says he won't trade for a thing that barely works. He scoops up his stones and moves toward the water butt, keeping his distance while Moll jeers from the wall

rulings.act: Give Cob the cricket and ask for another way in
rulings.why: the same push again, with nothing new
rulings.changed: the same answer as before: nothing changed

rulings.act: Bargain with Moll for a Saltmere curse
rulings.why: it costs them nothing (trivial, plausible, wary)
rulings.changed: Moll tilts her head, amused despite herself. “Fine. ‘Brenn’s barn,’” she says, giving you the dock-cant curse, then adds, “Now tell me about the bird.”
